rows.annotation: FAD-dependent dehydrogenase family protein, substrate undetermined.
rows.evidence: Query InterProScan identifies FAD-dependent protein and FAD/NAD(P)-binding domains. STRING COG2509 at 99.6% identity and Fitness Browser homolog annotations at 66.0–68.4% identity support an FAD-dependent dehydrogenase family assignment. Structural studies of the 68.7%-identity Vibrio homolog establish architecture but no catalytic substrate. No substrate-specific fitness measurements, biochemical assays, or EC assignments are supplied; cofitness correlations are modest (≤0.510), and conserved neighborhoods do not resolve function.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier B: homolog annotations and the STRING orthogroup support a dehydrogenase family, but no homolog has direct biochemical characterization establishing a specific substrate or reaction. Evidence includes structural and expression studies, query domains, homolog annotations, cofitness, neighborhoods, and topology; the experimental source labels do not establish substrate-specific activity. Specific disulfide reductase, amine oxidase, and BaiO assignments are unsupported because those suggestions lack corroborating query-specific catalytic evidence.

rows.kblh_paperblast_evidence:
PROTEIN SEQUENCE ORIGINATES FROM BACTERIA: Pseudomonas putida
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 68.70
Homolog originates from: Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD 2210633
Evidence type: computational
VP0956 is a protein from Vibrio parahaemolyticus; the paper specifically models its N-terminal domain (T0604_1). The authors show that SVMSEQ-generated contact predictions for this domain had high accuracy (72.9%), specifically along two β-sheets, which allowed I-TASSER to precisely pack three β-strands and achieve a TM-score of 0.691.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 68.70
Homolog originates from: Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD 2210633
Evidence type: experimental
The protein, also designated as target T0604, was experimentally determined to have three structural domains. The N-terminal domain (T0604_1) adopts a ferredoxin-like fold, the second domain (T0604_2) is a Rossmann-like FAD/NAD(P)-binding domain, and the third domain (T0604_3) is an α+β sandwich insertion. The paper details the specific secondary structure interactions, including a core antiparallel sheet and various helical and β-hairpin decorations in the T0604_3 domain.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 68.70
Homolog originates from: Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD 2210633
Evidence type: experimental
The N-terminal domain of this protein (T0604-D1) was used to evaluate the accuracy of sequence-based contact prediction. The paper demonstrates that SVMSEQ predicted 63 correct Cα contacting pairs, 55 of which were new contacts not found via threading. This sequence-based information allowed the Zhang-Server to build a high-resolution model with an RMSD of 2.66Å to the native structure, accurately packing three beta strands and two alpha helices.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 68.70
Homolog originates from: Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD 2210633
Evidence type: computational
The first domain of the VP0956 protein from Vibrio parahaemolyticus was used as a target for ab initio structural assembly using the QUARK program. The study used fragment-based distance profiles to identify eight correct long-range distance restraints, which helped the model correctly generate hydrogen bonds between the first and third β-strands and properly orient two short helices. The resulting model achieved a TM-score of 0.48 and an RMSD of 4.41 Å, although the C-terminal β-strand failed to form the native antiparallel β-sheet with the N-terminal β-strand.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 49.30
Homolog originates from: Clostridium thermocellum ATCC 27405
Evidence type: experimental
This gene encodes a FAD-dependent pyridine nucleotide-disulphide oxidoreductase. RNA-seq analysis showed it was downregulated in the evolved fructose-adapted strain (FAs8).
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 48.70
Homolog originates from: Clostridium botulinum D str. 1873
Evidence type: comparative
This gene, an NAD(P)/FAD-dependent oxidoreductase from Clostridium botulinum, was identified as differentially abundant, with higher representation in the control group relative to the treatment group (logFC 7.93, FDR 2.80E-04; Table 2, Fig 3B). It is categorized under COG H, which is involved in coenzyme transport and metabolism.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 47.80
Homolog originates from: Clostridium botulinum A str. ATCC 3502
Evidence type: experimental
Encodes an oxidoreductase. It was induced upon cold shock as part of the oxidative stress response.
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 46.50
Homolog originates from: Eggerthella lenta DSM 2243
Evidence type: comparative
This gene in E. lenta is identified as an ortholog of the proposed BaiO (CLOSCI_00522) with 45% identity and an e-value of e–126. It is co-localized with Elen_1017 and Elen_1016. Its protein is phylogenetically distant from BaiO proteins of Clostridiales.
[[END SUMMARY]]

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 37 (in 22 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 36 (21 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 37.9-99.6
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
